summary.headline: Balrampur Chini guides ~40% average PLA capacity utilisation for Jan-Mar 2027; sugar inventory of 45.67 lakh quintals carried at INR 37.19/kg as of June 30.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a tighter-than-expected sugar season, with lower production, healthy domestic consumption and ethanol diversion drawing down inventory, which firmed domestic sugar prices. Q1 FY27 is an off-season quarter with almost no production, so results depend on carrying cost and realisation of inventory; revenues rose in Sugar and Distillery on higher realisations and distillery volumes. The 80,000-tonne PLA plant is on track, with about INR 2,180 crore spent by end-July; lactic acid commissioning is guided for October and PLA for December. Management is not giving a quantified view on FY28 ethanol volumes or 2026-27 national sugar balance, pending policy and monsoon clarity around end-September.

financial_highlights.metric: Average carrying cost of sugar inventory

financial_highlights.value: Improved; figures not stated in call
financial_highlights.change: Higher sugar realisations and distillery volumes

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Q1 is off-season with largely no production; carrying cost and realisation of the 45.67 lakh quintal inventory drive quarterly profit. Management said sugar prices remain firm and inventory gives a favourable base for upcoming quarters. Sugar prices were cited at around INR 48-49 per kg.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Q1 margins described as resilient, helped by B-heavy and maize-based feedstock with hardly any juice-based sales. Management said some Maizapur costs were retained in the sugar division, so YoY comparison is not like-for-like.

segments.name: PLA (new, 80,000 tpa)
segments.commentary: Construction in full flow; lactic acid commissioning guided for October 2026 and PLA for December 2026. Guided average capacity utilisation of about 40% for Jan-Mar 2027, with target above that.

guidance_outlook: PLA: about 40% average capacity utilisation expected in Jan-Mar 2027, described as a safe expectation with target higher.
PLA commissioning: lactic acid in October 2026 and PLA in December 2026, per Chairman.

Sugar: management expects the inventory tightness to normalise in about one year if diversion is not allowed in 2026-27; cites a 31 mt production, 29 mt consumption and about 3 mt closing stock scenario, with stock normalisation around 1 October 2027 (45-50 lakh tonnes stock level).
Distillery FY28: if B-heavy and juice diversion is banned, management assumes only C-heavy is allowed; company said it is reworking numbers, and believes the net impact is positive.
Cane price hike expected; management assumes a sugarcane price increase and ban on diversion, and expects the net effect to be positive.
capex_capacity: 80,000-tonne PLA plant on track; INR 2,180 crore spent by end-July 2026.
Lactic acid plant commissioning targeted for October 2026; PLA for December 2026.
Analyst referenced INR 3,000-3,200 crore total capex; management said the capex could create a parallel Balrampur if PLA product lines scale.
Maizapur distillery is equipped for about 10 crore litres from grain; management said it is ready to make sugar if needed.
All units are equipped to produce C-heavy ethanol; crushing may reduce slightly at some units under a B-heavy ban, but targets are kept intact.
demand_pricing: Sugar prices moved up to around INR 48-49 per kg; management said the price base has moved up firmly and sustainably.
Management believes the market assumes closing stock lower than reality; a 2 million tonne variation between sources was called not possible.

Brazil production expected at around 40 million tonnes; ethanol more profitable there, so lower sugar diversion. EU sugar output contracting. Overall global deficit of 1-2 million tonnes per Pramod Patwari.
Broken rice policy may release about 15% of the food basket supply by Sept-Oct, per management's view; maize is market-driven.

PLA demand: management cites pan masala and gutka packaging shift after FSSAI/regulatory move; technical trials positive, outcome expected in 2-3 months. Straws and garbage bags already use PLA compounds.

qa_highlights.question: Could a B-heavy and juice diversion ban let distillery volumes reach about 10 crore litres from C-heavy plus 9-10 crore litres from grains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no B-heavy or juice diversion is a reasonable assumption for next season; only C-heavy allowed, and the C-heavy estimate is not far off. Grain volumes are market-driven, with broken rice availability expected after Sept-Oct policy. Numbers are being reworked.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLA commissioning timeline and first-year utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Lactic acid is expected in October and PLA in December; the chairman said output and quality timing are uncertain as it is a new business. Later, Avantika Saraogi guided about 40% average utilisation for Jan-Mar 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Can the pan masala/gutka packaging shift absorb full PLA capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the opportunity is large and that it could largely absorb capacity, but gave no verified tonnage numbers; FSSAI-related clarity expected in 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why were distillery margins resilient despite higher transfer prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Pramod Patwari said Q1 used mainly B-heavy and maize feedstock with little juice-based sales; Maizapur expenses were kept in sugar, so the comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: When will sugar inventory normalise and how long can high realisations last?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about one year, with normalisation around 1 October 2027 if diversion is not allowed; he expects prices above current levels in coming years.

risks_watch: Government policy on B-heavy and juice diversion, and grain (broken rice, maize) ethanol availability for the 2026-27 season.
Monsoon and cane yield clarity expected around end-September 2026; El Niño impact on recovery.
Cane price hike expected ahead of state elections, which could offset sugar price gains.
PLA commissioning timing, quality and utilisation; first-year ramp-up is unproven and management asked investors not to model Q1.
Regulatory treatment of PLA under the pan masala and gutka packaging rules remains unclear ("yes and no").
summary.management_tone: Confident and positive on sugar pricing and PLA prospects, but cautious and at times evasive on quantified numbers: management declined to give national sugar balance estimates, FY28 ethanol volumes, and PLA revenue, citing policy uncertainty.
key_quotes: As of June 30, the Company was carrying sugar inventory of 45.67 lakh quintals at an average carrying cost of INR 37.19 per kg.
A safe expectation maybe around 40% on average capacity utilization we should be able to achieve.
So, do not attempt, please, and this is a humble request, do not please attempt to put quarter one on it, at least.
Sugar price is the biggest delta in a company like ours or in any company.
